input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 meets the preferred position in full: we may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience (in whole or in part) on thirty days' written notice, we owe Fees only through the termination date, Vendor must refund prepaid Fees allocable to the post-termination period, and Vendor is expressly denied any convenience-termination right during a committed term. No early-termination fee or penalty appears anywhere (§ 27.3 likewise confirms termination "without penalty"), and no other clause gives Vendor a convenience or change-of-control exit (§ 24.4 bars a Vendor termination right on our change of control). Noting only, without flagging here: the § 2.1 take-or-pay commitment ("without reduction or termination rights") sits in tension with § 9.4's refund/fee-stop mechanics; that is the minimum-commitment term addressed under the MINCOMMIT rule and is not double-flagged under T4C.
